title: Conditional full-Q sector-weight non-identifiability bridge
purpose: Show that, when two fixed-Q component cylinder expectations differ, the absent sector-law input cannot be recovered uniquely from the component Gibbs family. The two delta laws are counterfactual admissible probability assignments used only as a separation proof; no PAH law is selected or instantiated.

fixed_scope.carrier_and_path: Use exactly the PAH-OMC-004 strip and the PAH-OMC-010 finite parameter path already inherited by PAH-OMC-012; this bridge takes no refinement, cutoff, volume, beta or observation limit.
fixed_scope.components: Use the unchanged PAH-001 fixed-Q component Gibbs functionals on the PAH-OMC-012 graded union. The index set contains Q=0 and Q=1 at n=2 because Q_n={0,...,2(n+2)}.
fixed_scope.cylinder: Use the declared grade-blind R-488 cylinder f=ell_a with anchor a=(0,0). It is bounded, gauge-invariant and anchor-preserving.
fixed_scope.component_values: The Q=0 component has phi_0(f)=0 because every nonnegative ell_v sums to zero. The Q=1 component has phi_1(f)>0 because an allowed finite configuration with ell_a=1 has strictly positive PAH Gibbs mass; R-492 records the corresponding value-1 finite-Gibbs-positive witness.
fixed_scope.counterfactual_weights: For the separation argument only, w^(0)=delta_Q=0 and w^(1)=delta_Q=1 are nonnegative normalized laws on the finite grade index. They are not source-owned, fitted, adopted, or used to define PAH-OMC-014.

lean.scope: Abstract finite convex mixtures: a zero component value and a strictly positive component value are separated by two normalized nonnegative delta weights. No PAH weight law is instantiated.

assumptions: A finite sector index type contains two grades q0 and q1.
Each component functional is already defined on the same cylinder f.
The q0 component value is exactly zero.
The q1 component value is strictly positive.
Only nonnegative normalized sector laws are admissible for the counterfactual comparison.
theorem_contract.conclusion: At least two admissible finite sector-weight laws give different values for f, so the component Gibbs family alone does not identify a unique full-Q mixture functional.
theorem_contract.PAH_instantiation: PAH-OMC-012/R-492 supplies the finite Q=0 zero fact and the Q=1 ell_a value-1 positive-mass witness; the strict expectation implication uses finite counting normalization and exp(-beta F)>0.

boundaries: This is an underdetermination theorem, not a source-owned sector law and not a choice of weights.
It does not prove that every future cross-Q law fails projective consistency; it proves only that the current component data do not select one uniquely.
It does not supply a Cauchy error, a weak cylinder limit, R-488 global nonzero, stationarity, closability or an infinite-volume state.
R-484 defect 16/9 and R-490 C_sw=540 are untouched and are not used as a weight or limit estimate.
adversarial_firewall: Do not relabel delta_Q=0 or delta_Q=1 as the PAH source law.
Do not fit weights to the target cylinder or observation data.
Do not use a component witness as a global nonzero limit.
Do not promote this finite identifiability result to physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, Yang--Mills, continuum, mass-gap or TOE evidence.
missing_inputs: A source-authorized hash-pinned full-Q sector law or equivalent projective kernel.
A common cylinder topology and PAH-specific Cauchy error under the fixed PAH-001 order.
A domain and uniform-integrability estimate for the stationarity identity.

next_question: Can a source owner provide one exact normalized w_(n,R,Q) or projective cross-Q kernel, with topology and Cauchy bound, so that the already-proved conditional separation is no longer an underdetermined counterfactual?
non_claims: No full-Q Gibbs state, projective limit or omega is defined.
No infinite-volume semigroup, quantum real-time dynamics, physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, Yang--Mills, mass-gap or TOE conclusion follows.
Markov time remains external stochastic time.
